segments.label: PAPER
segments.headline: How Apple's robot practiced in pretend homes

beats.narration: Many robots learn by copying a person who steers them, and that takes lots of people's time. So how do you train one with nobody steering?
Apple researchers built a kind of flight simulator for robots.
A computer makes up a home and plans the robot's moves,
then draws what its camera would see, home after home.
And in real homes it had never seen, it got most simple tasks right.
The paper's point: this practice grows with computing power, not people's time.

visual.text: More computers, not more people's time
visual.sub: The paper: data “scales with compute rather than human labor”

beats.narration: But it's an early paper, with the team's own tests.
